title: 7.7 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can draw polygons from their vertex coordinates on the coordinate plane, and use coordinates to find side lengths and solve perimeter and area problems, explain what each part stands for, and build one for a situation I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

noticeAndWonder.context: A town-planning map shows a grid with two corner points of a future rectangular park already marked. The rest of the park is drawn only as a dashed outline waiting for its other two corners.
noticeStarters: I notice the two marked points share ___ .
I notice each grid square stands for ___ .
wonderStarters: I wonder where the other corners ___ .
noticeAndWonder.imageAlt: A town-planning grid with two surveyed park corners marked at negative 4, 3 and 5, negative 3, and the rest of the rectangle drawn as a dashed outline with two unmarked corners.
noticeAndWonder.contextEs: Un mapa de planeación urbana muestra una cuadrícula con dos puntos de esquina de un futuro parque rectangular ya marcados. El resto del parque está dibujado solo como un contorno punteado esperando sus otras dos esquinas.
noticeAndWonder.imageAltEs: Una cuadrícula de planeación urbana con dos esquinas de parque ya medidas y marcadas en menos 4, 3 y en 5, menos 3, y el resto del rectángulo dibujado como un contorno punteado con dos esquinas sin marcar.
noticeStartersEs: Yo noto que los dos puntos marcados comparten ___ .
Yo noto que cada cuadro de la cuadrícula representa ___ .
Yo noto que el contorno punteado ___ .

vocabulary.definition: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair on the coordinate plane.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un punto de esquina de un polígono, nombrado por un par ordenado en el plano de coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: The park's corner at (2, 4) — one corner, named by an ordered pair.
vocabulary.cloze: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair, is a ___.

examples.text: (5, 4), where two sides of the park meet
examples.why: It is a corner, and a coordinate pair names it.
That is a side; a vertex is the point where sides meet.

vocabulary.definition: A closed figure made of line segments; on the plane you draw it by plotting the vertices and connecting them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura cerrada hecha de segmentos; en el plano se dibuja marcando los vértices y conectándolos en orden.
vocabulary.example: Plot the four points, connect them, and the rectangle appears.
vocabulary.visual: Plot (2, 4), (5, 4), (5, −4), (2, −4) and join them — a rectangle appears.
vocabulary.cloze: A closed figure made of line segments is a ___.

examples.text: Four plotted vertices joined in order into a closed rectangle
examples.why: Straight sides, and the figure closes.

examples.text: Three points joined but left open
examples.why: An unclosed path is not a polygon.

vocabulary.definition: The total distance around a polygon — the sum of all its side lengths.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia total alrededor de un polígono: la suma de todos sus lados.
vocabulary.cloze: The total distance around a polygon is its ___.

examples.text: Adding all four side lengths of the rectangle
examples.why: It measures the whole way around.
That gives area — the space inside, not the distance around.

vocabulary.definition: When two vertices share an x- or y-coordinate, the distance between them is the absolute difference of the other coordinates.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando dos vértices comparten una coordenada x o y, la distancia es la diferencia absoluta de las otras coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: (2, 4) and (5, 4) share y, so the side is |5 − 2| = 3 units.
vocabulary.cloze: When two vertices share a coordinate, subtract the other and take the ___ ___.

examples.text: |4 − (−4)| = 8 for two vertices that share an x-value
examples.why: Same x means a vertical side, found by subtracting the y-values.
Losing the negative sign collapses the side to nothing.

vocabulary.definition: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que representa una unidad de la cuadrícula en la situación real.
vocabulary.example: Each unit is 100 feet, so 3 units of width is 300 feet.
vocabulary.visual: Each grid unit = 100 feet, so 8 units of map is 800 real feet.
vocabulary.cloze: What one grid unit stands for in the real situation is the ___.

examples.text: 1 unit = 100 feet on the park map
examples.why: It converts grid units into real distance.

examples.text: The number of units between two vertices
examples.why: That is a length on the grid; the scale is what a unit means.

turnAndTalk.question: The vertices (-4.5, 3) and (5, 3) share y = 3, so the side between them is horizontal, with length |5 − (−4.5)| = 9.5. Why is that side's length found by comparing the x-coordinates instead of the y-coordinates?
turnAndTalk.kernel: When two vertices share the same y-coordinate, the segment between them is horizontal, so its length comes from the DIFFERENCE in the coordinate that changes — the x-coordinates.

stems.en: The side is horizontal because both vertices share the same ___-coordinate.
stems.es: El lado es horizontal porque ambos vértices comparten la misma coordenada ___.

stems.en: I subtract the ___-coordinates because that's the coordinate that ___.
stems.es: Resto las coordenadas ___ porque esa es la coordenada que ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Vertices (5, 3) and (5, -3.75) share x = 5 instead. Justify why the distance between them is |3 − (−3.75)| = 6.75 and not just 3.75 − 3.
extendStems: The distance is 6.75, not 0.75, because the segment crosses ___, so you add the distance from 3 to 0 and from 0 to ___.
Using absolute value matters here because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: You sorted pairs of vertices into 'subtract coordinates' versus 'slanted.' How did you decide that (0, 0) and (4, 3) belonged in the slanted group?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Coordinates can be subtracted directly only when two vertices share an x-value or a y-value; if BOTH coordinates differ, the segment is slanted and this lesson's subtraction method doesn't apply.

stems.en: (0, 0) and (4, 3) are slanted because they don't share the same ___ or the same ___.
stems.es: (0, 0) y (4, 3) están inclinados porque no comparten la misma ___ ni la misma ___.

stems.en: (-4, 1) and (6, 1) belong with 'subtract coordinates' because they share ___.
stems.es: (-4, 1) y (6, 1) van con 'restar coordenadas' porque comparten ___.

turnAndTalk.extend: Explain why a rectangle drawn from four vertices will always have sides you CAN find by subtracting coordinates, even though a slanted pair exists elsewhere on the same grid.
extendStems: A rectangle's sides always share a coordinate because ___.
The diagonal of the rectangle would be slanted because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The Town Square park's two known vertices are 3 units apart, and each unit represents 100 feet, so the width is 300 feet. The park's area must be 240,000 square feet. How do you use that to find how many units below the known vertices the missing vertices go?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Length = area ÷ width gives 800 feet, and dividing that by the 100-feet-per-unit scale converts it to 8 map units.

stems.en: Converting to map units, I divide ___ feet by ___ to get ___ units.
stems.es: Al convertir a unidades del mapa, divido ___ pies entre ___ para obtener ___ unidades.

turnAndTalk.extend: Explain why dividing by 100 (the scale) is necessary at the end, instead of just using the 800 feet directly as the number of units to move on the grid.
extendStems: The scale tells us that one grid unit equals ___ feet, so we must ___ before placing the new vertices.

turnAndTalk.question: Look back at a problem where you found the perimeter of a rectangle from its vertices. What were your steps from the coordinates to the final perimeter?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Finding a rectangle's perimeter from vertices means finding two different side lengths using coordinate subtraction, then computing 2(length) + 2(width).

stems.en: First I found the width using vertices ___ and ___, which gave ___ units.
stems.es: Primero encontré el ancho usando los vértices ___ y ___, lo cual dio ___ unidades.

turnAndTalk.extend: A classmate computed the perimeter of a rectangle with sides 9.5 and 6.75 as 9.5 × 6.75 = 64.125. What did they compute instead, and how would you help them fix it?
extendStems: They computed the ___ of the rectangle instead of the perimeter.
I would tell them perimeter means adding around the outside, so it should be 2(___) + 2(___) instead of multiplying.

launch.narrative: This is your challenge small group for Lesson 7.7. You can already get the answer — so in here the answer is the starting point. We ask when the method holds, when it breaks, and how you would convince someone who disagrees.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — The coordinates already know the side lengths
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: When two vertices share a coordinate, the side between them is the absolute difference of the coordinates that differ — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

iDo.title: Watch me find one side
lines: (-4.5, 3) and (5, 3) share y = 3, so the side between them is horizontal.
Its length is the distance between the x-coordinates: |5 − (−4.5)| = 9.5 units.
(5, 3) and (5, -3.75) share x = 5, so that side is vertical: |3 − (−3.75)| = 6.75 units.
linesEs: (-4.5, 3) y (5, 3) comparten y = 3, así que el lado entre ellos es horizontal.
Su longitud es la distancia entre las coordenadas x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 9.5 unidades.
(5, 3) y (5, -3.75) comparten x = 5, así que ese lado es vertical: |3 − (−3.75)| = 6.75 unidades.

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: The shape is a rectangle, so the opposite sides match: two sides of 9.5 and two of 6.75.
That is why two of the terms are multiplied by 2 — each length appears on two sides.
Now prove it: say why that move had to work at all — not just that it did.
Sentence frame — convince a skeptic: "My method works because ___ . It would stop working if ___ ."
linesEs: La figura es un rectángulo, así que los lados opuestos coinciden: dos lados de 9.5 y dos de 6.75.
Por eso dos de los términos se multiplican por 2 — cada longitud aparece en dos lados.
Ahora demuéstralo: di por qué ese paso tenía que funcionar — no solo que funcionó.
Marco de oración — convence a alguien que duda: «Mi método funciona porque ___ . Dejaría de funcionar si ___ .»

youDo.title: Now you try — and defend it
lines: Try the problems below on your own. Getting the answer is half the work — be ready to say why your method works, and where it would stop working.
Then pick one problem and show it a second way. If two different methods agree, that agreement is your proof.
linesEs: Intenta los problemas de abajo por tu cuenta. Obtener la respuesta es la mitad del trabajo — prepárate para decir por qué funciona tu método y dónde dejaría de funcionar.
Luego elige un problema y muéstralo de una segunda manera. Si dos métodos distintos coinciden, esa coincidencia es tu prueba.

conceptIntro.headingEs: Ve más allá — Las coordenadas ya saben las longitudes de los lados
conceptIntro.introEs: Esto ya lo sabes hacer. Así que subimos de nivel, no de número: halla lo que siempre es cierto, muéstralo de una segunda manera y prepárate para defenderlo con una razón en lugar de una respuesta.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Cuando dos vértices comparten una coordenada, el lado entre ellos es la diferencia absoluta de las coordenadas que cambian — y puedes decir por qué es cierto y dónde dejaría de serlo.

explore.label: Sort each pair of vertices: can you find the distance between them by SUBTRACTING COORDINATES, or would the segment be slanted (not this lesson's tool)?
categories: Same x or same y — subtract coordinates
Slanted — coordinates alone won't give it yet
explore.instructions: Go deeper: Sort all eight, then pick one 'subtract' pair and say the distance out loud with its absolute-value sentence. As you work, ask yourself WHY it works.

diagram.title: Plot the Park Rectangle
diagram.caption: P and Q share y = 1, so PQ = |6 - (-4)| = 10 units. Q and R share x = 6, so QR = |1 - (-3)| = 4 units. Perimeter = 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 units.
diagram.captionEs: P y Q comparten y = 1, así que PQ = |6 - (-4)| = 10 unidades. Q y R comparten x = 6, así que QR = |1 - (-3)| = 4 unidades. Perímetro = 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 unidades.

explore.instructionsEs: Ve más a fondo: Clasifica las ocho y luego escoge un par de «restar» y di la distancia en voz alta con su oración de valor absoluto. Mientras trabajas, pregúntate por qué funciona.
explore.labelEs: Clasifica cada par de vértices: ¿puedes hallar la distancia entre ellos restando coordenadas, o el segmento quedaría inclinado (que no es la herramienta de esta lección)?

connect.scenario: Designing the Town Square: a rectangular park will have an area of 240,000 square feet. Two vertices are already marked on the planning grid, 3 units apart, and each grid unit represents 100 feet.
connect.promptQuestion: Where do the other two vertices go — and how do the known coordinates, the scale, and the area work together to tell you?
connect.prompt: The park's width is ___ feet. Using the area formula, its length is ___ feet, which is ___ units on the map — so the new vertices sit that many units below the known ones.

check.stem: The two known vertices of the park are 3 units apart, and each grid unit represents 100 feet. What is the park's width in feet?
check.explanation: Multiply the unit distance by the scale: 3 units × 100 feet per unit = 300 feet. Leaving off the scale (3 feet) or adding instead of multiplying (103 feet) ignores what the scale means.

check.stem: The park's area must be 240,000 sq ft and its width is 300 ft. What is its length?
check.explanation: Length = area ÷ width = 240,000 ÷ 300 = 800 feet. Adding the width to the area (240,300) confuses two different operations — area and length combine here by division, not addition.

check.stem: The park's length is 800 feet, and each grid unit represents 100 feet. How many units below the known vertices do the new corners sit?
check.explanation: Convert feet back to units by dividing by the scale: 800 ÷ 100 = 8 units. Dividing by 10 instead of 100 gives 80, and skipping the conversion entirely leaves the answer in feet (800), not map units.

connect.modelAnswer: The marked vertices are 3 units apart, and each unit is 100 feet, so the width is 300 feet. The area must be 240,000 square feet, so the length is 240,000 ÷ 300 = 800 feet. Dividing by the scale, 800 ÷ 100 = 8 units, so the other two vertices go 8 units below the known vertices.

diagram.title: Perimeter of the Rectangle (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1), (−3, −1)
diagram.caption: The two horizontal sides are each |4 − (−3)| = 7 units and the two vertical sides are each |2 − (−1)| = 3 units, so the perimeter is 7 + 7 + 3 + 3 = 20 units.

onLevel.stem: The park's marked vertices are 3 units apart and each unit is 100 feet. What is the park's width?
choiceFeedback: 3 is the number of UNITS — the scale turns units into feet.
That adds 3 + 100 instead of multiplying.
That multiplies by 10 instead of 100.
hints: What does one unit stand for?
Each unit is 100 feet.
onLevel.stemEs: Los vértices marcados del parque están a 3 unidades de distancia y cada unidad son 100 pies. ¿Cuál es el ancho del parque?
hintsEs: ¿Qué representa una unidad?
Cada unidad son 100 pies.

onLevel.stem: The park's area must be 240,000 sq ft and its width is 300 ft. What is its length?
choiceFeedback: That divides by 3 instead of 300 — keep the zeros with the width.
720 comes from 240,000 ÷ 333 or a slip; recompute 240,000 ÷ 300.
That adds the width to the area — area and length combine by division here.
hints: Area = length × width. Solve for length.
24,000 ÷ 30 is the same division.
onLevel.stemEs: El área del parque debe ser 240,000 pies cuadrados y su ancho es 300 pies. ¿Cuál es su largo?
hintsEs: Área = largo × ancho. Despeja el largo.
24,000 ÷ 30 es la misma división.

onLevel.stem: The length is 800 feet and each unit represents 100 feet. How many units long is the park on the map?
choiceFeedback: That divides by 10 instead of 100.
That forgets the scale entirely — the map is not drawn in feet.
That divides by 1,000 instead of 100.
hints: Feet to units: divide by what one unit stands for.
Move the decimal two places.
onLevel.stemEs: El largo es 800 pies y cada unidad representa 100 pies. ¿Cuántas unidades de largo mide el parque en el mapa?
hintsEs: De pies a unidades: divide entre lo que representa una unidad.
Mueve el decimal dos lugares.

onLevel.stem: The known vertices of the park are at (2, 4) and (5, 4), and the length runs DOWNWARD 8 units. Where are the other two vertices?
onLevel.explanation: 8 units below y = 4 is y = 4 − 8 = −4, keeping each x the same: (2, −4) and (5, −4).
choiceFeedback: (2, 12) moves UP 8 units instead of down.
Those move sideways along x instead of down.
y = −8 would be 12 units below y = 4, not 8.
hints: Down means subtract from y.
x-coordinates stay the same.
onLevel.stemEs: Los vértices conocidos del parque están en (2, 4) y (5, 4), y el largo va HACIA ABAJO 8 unidades. ¿Dónde están los otros dos vértices?
onLevel.explanationEs: 8 unidades debajo de y = 4 es y = 4 − 8 = −4, manteniendo igual cada x: (2, −4) y (5, −4).
hintsEs: Hacia abajo significa restar de y.
Las coordenadas x se quedan igual.

extending.label: Find the distance between each pair of vertices.
extending.labelEs: Halla la distancia entre cada par de vértices.
hints: Distance across zero adds the two distances from the axis: from −4 to 5 is 4 + 5.
Subtract when signs match, add absolute values when the points sit on opposite sides of the axis.
hintsEs: La distancia que cruza el cero suma las dos distancias desde el eje: de −4 a 5 es 4 + 5.
Resta cuando los signos coinciden; suma los valores absolutos cuando los puntos están en lados opuestos del eje.
extending.explanation: From (−4, 3) to (5, 3): the x-values sit on opposite sides of zero, so the distance is 4 + 5 = 9. From (5, 3) to (5, −4): 3 + 4 = 7. From (−2, −1) to (6, −1): 2 + 6 = 8. Coordinates turn side lengths into arithmetic — no ruler required.
extending.explanationEs: De (−4, 3) a (5, 3): los valores de x están en lados opuestos del cero, así que la distancia es 4 + 5 = 9. De (5, 3) a (5, −4): 3 + 4 = 7. De (−2, −1) a (6, −1): 2 + 6 = 8. Las coordenadas convierten las longitudes en aritmética: no hace falta regla.

extending.instructions: Plot the four vertices of rectangle PQRS: P(1, 2), Q(6, 2), R(6, 5), S(1, 5).
extending.instructionsEs: Ubica los cuatro vértices del rectángulo PQRS: P(1, 2), Q(6, 2), R(6, 5), S(1, 5).
extending.label: Plot the vertices of rectangle PQRS, then use the coordinates to find its perimeter.
extending.labelEs: Ubica los vértices del rectángulo PQRS y luego usa las coordenadas para hallar su perímetro.
hints: Move right for x first, then up for y — every vertex starts at the origin.
After plotting, subtract coordinates: PQ shares y = 2, so its length is 6 − 1 = 5.
hintsEs: Muévete a la derecha para x primero y luego hacia arriba para y: cada vértice empieza en el origen.
Después de ubicar, resta coordenadas: PQ comparte y = 2, así que su longitud es 6 − 1 = 5.
extending.explanation: P and Q share y = 2, so PQ = 6 − 1 = 5 units; Q and R share x = 6, so QR = 5 − 2 = 3 units. The rectangle is 5 by 3, giving perimeter 2 × (5 + 3) = 16 units and area 5 × 3 = 15 square units — all read straight off the coordinates.
extending.explanationEs: P y Q comparten y = 2, así que PQ = 6 − 1 = 5 unidades; Q y R comparten x = 6, así que QR = 5 − 2 = 3 unidades. El rectángulo mide 5 por 3, con perímetro 2 × (5 + 3) = 16 unidades y área 5 × 3 = 15 unidades cuadradas: todo se lee directo de las coordenadas.

extending.stem: A rectangle has vertices (-3, 2), (4, 2), (4, -1), (-3, -1). What is its perimeter?
choiceFeedback: 10 is 7 + 3 — only two of the four sides.
21 is 7 × 3 — the area, not the perimeter.
13 misreads one of the distances; recompute both using absolute differences.
hints: Find both side lengths from the coordinates first.
Width 7, height 3.
extending.stemEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (-3, 2), (4, 2), (4, -1), (-3, -1). ¿Cuál es su perímetro?
extending.explanationEs: Ancho |4 − (−3)| = 7, alto |2 − (−1)| = 3, así que P = 2(7) + 2(3) = 20 unidades.
hintsEs: Halla primero las dos longitudes de los lados a partir de las coordenadas.
Ancho 7, alto 3.

extending.stem: Sheng plans a zoo visit using a map where exhibits sit at grid points. Explain how identifying WHAT the problem asks (his shortest route? total distance?) changes what you compute.
extending.modelAnswer: If the problem asks total walking distance, I add the distances between the exhibits along his path. If it asks whether one route is shorter than another, I compute both totals and compare. Naming the question first tells me which distances matter.
sentenceStems: If the question is ___ , I would compute ___ .
Identifying the problem first helps because ___ .
extending.stemEs: Sheng planea una visita al zoológico usando un mapa donde las exhibiciones están en puntos de la cuadrícula. Explica cómo identificar QUÉ pide el problema (¿su ruta más corta? ¿la distancia total?) cambia lo que calculas.
sentenceStemsEs: Si la pregunta es ___ , yo calcularía ___ .
Identificar el problema primero ayuda porque ___ .

extending.stem: Vertices (−2, 6) and (−2, −6): the distance between them is
choiceFeedback: The points are different — sharing an x does not make the distance zero.
4 subtracts 6 − 2, mixing the x into it.
36 multiplies 6 × 6 instead of finding the gap.
hints: Which coordinate differs?
6 and −6.
6 above zero plus 6 below.
extending.stemEs: Los vértices (−2, 6) y (−2, −6): la distancia entre ellos es
extending.explanationEs: La misma x, así que la distancia = |6 − (−6)| = 12 unidades.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada es distinta?
6 arriba del cero más 6 abajo.

extending.stem: Maria is choosing between two store spaces on a grid where each unit is 1 foot and each grid line is 5 feet apart. Space A is a rectangle 25 ft by 40 ft; Space B is 30 ft by 30 ft. Which has more floor area?
choices: Space A — 1,000 sq ft vs 900 sq ft
Space B — 900 sq ft vs 850 sq ft
Space B — because a square always beats a rectangle
extending.explanation: A: 25 × 40 = 1,000 sq ft. B: 30 × 30 = 900 sq ft. Space A has 100 more square feet.
choiceFeedback: B is 900, but A is 1,000 — recompute 25 × 40.
Shape does not decide area; the dimensions do.
hints: Compute each area.
extending.stemEs: María escoge entre dos locales en una cuadrícula donde cada unidad es 1 pie y cada línea está a 5 pies de distancia. El espacio A es un rectángulo de 25 pies por 40 pies; el espacio B es de 30 pies por 30 pies. ¿Cuál tiene más área de piso?
extending.explanationEs: A: 25 × 40 = 1,000 pies cuadrados. B: 30 × 30 = 900 pies cuadrados. El espacio A tiene 100 pies cuadrados más.
hintsEs: Calcula cada área.
choicesEs: Espacio A — 1,000 pies cuadrados vs 900 pies cuadrados
Espacio B — 900 pies cuadrados vs 850 pies cuadrados
Espacio B — porque un cuadrado siempre le gana a un rectángulo

extending.stem: A square has vertices (a, b) and (a, b + s) on one side. Which operation gives the side length for ANY values?
choices: Subtract the y-coordinates and take the absolute value
extending.explanation: Same x means the side is vertical, and |(b + s) − b| = |s| — subtraction with absolute value works for every case.
choiceFeedback: Adding coordinates has no geometric meaning here.
A product of coordinates is not a distance.
An average finds a midpoint, not a length.
hints: Which coordinate changes along the side?
Only y changes.
Distance = absolute difference of the changing coordinate.
extending.stemEs: Un cuadrado tiene los vértices (a, b) y (a, b + s) en un lado. ¿Cuál operación da la longitud del lado para CUALQUIER valor?
extending.explanationEs: La misma x significa que el lado es vertical, y |(b + s) − b| = |s| — la resta con valor absoluto funciona en todos los casos.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada cambia a lo largo del lado?
Solo cambia y.
Distancia = diferencia absoluta de la coordenada que cambia.
choicesEs: Restar las coordenadas y y tomar el valor absoluto
Saca el promedio de las coordenadas

extending.stem: The park design used width from coordinates, then length from the area, then the scale to place the missing vertices. Design your own version: pick an area and a scale, mark two vertices, and show where the other two go.
extending.modelAnswer: My park has area 60,000 sq ft with each unit = 100 ft. I mark vertices at (1, 5) and (3, 5) — 2 units apart, so width 200 ft. Length = 60,000 ÷ 200 = 300 ft = 3 units, so the other vertices go at (1, 2) and (3, 2), 3 units below.
sentenceStems: My area is ___ and each unit is ___ .
So the other vertices are at ___ .
extending.stemEs: El diseño del parque usó el ancho de las coordenadas, luego el largo del área, y luego la escala para ubicar los vértices que faltaban. Diseña tu propia versión: escoge un área y una escala, marca dos vértices y muestra dónde van los otros dos.
sentenceStemsEs: Mi área es ___ y cada unidad es ___ .
Así que los otros vértices están en ___ .

extending.title: Fix our table's thinking

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: A rectangle has vertices (-3, 2), (4, 2), (4, -1), (-3, -1). What is its perimeter?
workedExample.workEs: Un rectángulo tiene vértices (-3, 2), (4, 2), (4, -1), (-3, -1). ¿Cuál es su perímetro?

workedExample.label: A classmate at our table answered
workedExample.labelEs: Un compañero de nuestra mesa respondió

extending.correctWork: The correct answer is 20 units. Width |4 − (−3)| = 7, height |2 − (−1)| = 3, so P = 2(7) + 2(3) = 20 units.
extending.correctWorkEs: La respuesta correcta es 20 unidades. Ancho |4 − (−3)| = 7, alto |2 − (−1)| = 3, así que P = 2(7) + 2(3) = 20 unidades.
hints: Find both side lengths from the coordinates first.
hintsEs: Halla primero las dos longitudes de los lados a partir de las coordenadas.

practice.commonMistake: Subtracting coordinates without the absolute value — from y = 3 down to y = −3.75 the distance is 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units, not 3.75 − 3 = 0.75. Distances that cross zero are the whole reason the absolute value is there.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A rectangle has vertices (-1, 4), (5, 4), (5, 1), (-1, 1). What is its perimeter?

parallelPractice.stem: Plot and name the quadrant for the new point (1, -1).
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: Move horizontally to x = 1.
parallelPractice.explanation: Move horizontally to x = 1. Move vertically to y = -1. Name the quadrant: Quadrant IV.
parallelPractice.stemEs: Ubica y nombra el cuadrante del nuevo punto (1, -1).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Usa el modelo visual y completa un paso a la vez.
Empieza así: Muévete horizontalmente hasta x = 1.
